comments.text: One important thing to note for people reading this is that hyperactivity doesn't always persist into adulthood with the other symptoms or is greatly reduced and is often turned inward (mental fidgeting). As far as your firings go, if you haven't watched this video and/or read this doctor's books they really help with understanding exactly what you're dealing with: [VIDEO] It's long but worth watching at faster playback speed and in manageable chunks. Key takeaways: "Attention deficit" is less of a symptom and more of a measurable consequence of other symptoms: Impaired inhibition/impulse control, excessive irrelevant activity and impaired persistence (think discipline). Once you understand why you fail you can start addressing or working around your gaps, particularly the ones that any medication you may be on fail to address.

comments.text_zh: ADHD 这个名字起得非常糟糕，而且在成年人身上通常并不表现为身体上的多动。它是一种执行功能障碍。这意味着诸如时间盲——难以把任务概念化并持续推向未来，以及难以把短期目标记在脑子里。我把它想成丢包，但丢的是意图。执行功能健康时，一个人的目标和意图是持续的数据流，可以像铁轨一样一直抓着。（这是基于别人对自己头脑运作方式的描述——我会把这种能力视为超能力。）有 ADHD 时，轨道会时不时像活板门一样塌掉——有时每隔几秒就塌一次。你必须重新建立连接，但因为出故障的东西正是那个记得要连接什么的东西，所以我得重新确认自己一开始想做什么，而通常那已经不是我之前在做的事了。所以我最后只能以半高效的爆发方式到处乱射，无法把事情做完。另一个反直觉的地方是过度专注——有 ADHD 的人会周期性地体验到相反的状态。过去三天里，我几乎每个清醒的时刻都在专心做一个我感兴趣的软件项目。短时间的强烈专注（尤其是如果你觉得自己并不能控制它何时发生）并不意味着你没有 ADHD。它们可能意味着相反的情况。这是我见过的对这个主题最好的解释：[VIDEO]
comments.text: ADHD is terribly misnamed, and doesn't usually manifest as physical hyperactivity in adults. It's an executive function disorder. This means things like time blindness – difficulty conceptualizing and persisting tasks into the future, and difficulty keeping short term goals in mind. I think about it like packet loss, but for intent. With healthy executive function, one's goals and intents are persistent streams that can be held on to like a train track. (This is based on other people's description of how their mind works – I would consider that ability a superpower). With ADHD, the tracks will just fall out like a trapdoor every so often – sometimes every few seconds. You have to reinitiate the connection, but because the thing that failed is the same thing that remembers what to connect to, I have to reestablish what I want to do in the first place, and it's usually not the thing I was doing before. So I end up shooting around in semi-productive bursts, unable to see things to completion. The other counterintuitive thing is hyperfocus – people with ADHD periodically experience the inverse. I spent nearly every waking moment in the last 3 days working intently on a software project I'm interested in. Short bouts of intense concentration (especially if you don't feel in control of their application) do not mean you don't have ADHD. They could mean the opposite. Here's the best explanation I've ever seen of the subject: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 这是 FUD。ADHD 已经被充分研究，也被研究它的人很好地理解。问题在于，人们以为 ADHD 只是自律或注意力的问题。并不是。它是一种严重的障碍，会带来明确而严重的影响。毫无疑问，有些人为了拿到兴奋剂而声称自己有 ADHD；而没有 ADHD 的人声称自己有 ADHD，可能会让人以为这种障碍模棱两可，但其实并非如此。另外，如果一个人长期有 ADHD，可能会与其他障碍共病，比如抑郁症等，这也会让人们的看法变得模糊。ADHD 严格来说不是注意力问题。它以注意力命名，是因为那是一个早期且明显的症状，但它比这严重得多。把这个障碍叫作注意力缺陷障碍，结果非常糟糕，因为它会让人们对这种障碍形成错误的心智模型。以为这只是患者本人的懒惰，或者如果是儿童，就是患者父母的懒惰。这是一种可悲的、被误导的看法，源于无知和糟糕的命名。实际上，ADHD 是一种发育性障碍，是执行功能更广泛的受损；除了注意力不集中之外，还包括情绪调节、工作记忆、对时间的内部感知以及其他影响。这种受损是由多巴胺转运异常造成的，这一点可以在 MRI 研究中清楚地观察到。这些研究已经被重复了很多次，在 m
comments.text: This is FUD. ADHD is well researched, and well understood by those who study it. The problem is that people think ADHD is just an issue of self discipline or attentiveness. It is not. It is a serious disorder with serious effects that are unambiguous. No doubt there are stimulant seeking people who claim to have ADHD to get stimulants, and people without ADHD representing that they have ADHD may lead to the impression that the disorder is ambiguous when it isn't. Also if someone has ADHD for long periods of time they may have co-mobidity with other disorders such as depression, etc. and this also may muddy perceptions. ADHD is not strictly an attention issue. It's named for attention because that is an early and obvious symptom but it is much worse then that. Calling the disorder an attention deficit disorder has turned out to be very bad as it leads people to the wrong mental model of the disorder. Thinking that it's just laziness on the part of the patent or the patents parents, in the case of children. This is a tragically misguided perception, based in ignorance and the poor choice of names. In actuality ADHD is a developmental disorder that is a more general impairment of executive function that includes regulation of emotion, working memory and the internal perception of time and other effects in addition to inattentiveness. comments.text_zh: 我非常同意，也有类似的经历。与 ADHD 作斗争并不是能不能集中注意力的问题。部分问题在于，要把注意力指向并保持在那些不愉快的任务上，而与之对抗的是一个长期多巴胺和去甲肾上腺素传递偏低的大脑。作为一个已确诊并接受治疗的 ADHD 患者，这些文章是误导性的。在我看来，宣称“做这一件行为上的事，你的 ADHD 就会消失（或变得更容易）”是危险的。在与 ADHD 斗争了 25 年以上之后，我可以告诉你：这些生活小妙招没用。请去咨询医疗专业人士。这会为你省下多年的痛苦和失望。再说一遍，如果你有——或怀疑自己有——ADHD，请与精神科医生合作，讨论诊断和治疗方案。就这样。引用 Russell Barkeley 博士的话：“ADHD 是理解得最清楚的精神疾病之一，如果不是最清楚的话。我们理解它已有几十年了——它也被称为精神科中的糖尿病，因为有治疗方法”[^1]。所以，我们知道它是什么，也早就知道该怎么治疗它。这是一种神经遗传疾病，而且我们已经有有效的药物——我想——有 50 年了，包括显而易见的 methylphenidate 和 dexamphetamines。读完这篇文章以及许多类似文章后，我感到沮丧，因为我认为它们是掠夺性的。它们瞄准的是像我这样的神经多样性人群。天哪，我确实一次又一次掉进那些陷阱，直到我真正开始接受医学治疗。我猜想 Jacqueline 写作并发表
comments.text: I very much agree and share a similar experience. Struggling with ADHD is not a matter of not being able to focus. Part of the issue is directing and keeping attention on non-pleasant tasks that are stacked up against a brain chronically low on dopamine and norepinephrine transmission. As someone with diagnosed and treated ADHD, these articles are misleading. In my opinion it's dangerous to claim "Do this ONE behavioural thing and your ADHD goes away (or gets easier.)" After struggling with ADHD for 25+ years I can tell you: These life-hacks don't work. Please, consult with a medical professional instead. It'll save you years of agony and disappointment. Again, if you have – or suspect – ADHD, work with a psychiatrist to discuss diagnosis and treatment options. Period. Quoting Dr. Russell Barkeley "ADHD is one, if not the best-understood psychiatric conditions. We understand it for several decades now - it's also called the diabetes of psychiatry because there's treatment"[^1]. So, we know what it is and have known how to treat it. It's a neuro-genetic disease, and we have had working medications for – I think – 50 years including the obvious methylphenidate and dexamphetamines. After reading the article and so many like it, I feel frustrated because I think they're predatory. They're targeting neuro-divergent people like myself. comments.text_zh: > 还没拿到我的新处方（昨天吃完了），但除此之外，我每天服用 30mg dexedrine XR。嘿，一样。我昨天吃完了药，也还没拿到新处方。这个月让我不爽的是，我只拿到了 28 天的药量，这也太小气了——大多数超过 30 天的月份我都没拿到 31 天的量！不过算了，撇开这个不说，我很高兴自己在英国，每月花十英镑就能拿到每天 108mg methylphenidate 和每天 10mg Ramipril。 > 我一直被推荐试试 ritalin/methylphenidate，我确实计划某个时候试试，但 dexedrine 对我帮助太大了，我觉得我不需要换别的。不过我还是想试试 methylphenidate，看看感觉如何。要注意，和 dexedrine 相比，你可能会觉得它没那么惊艳，效果在当下远没有那么明显——事实上，methylphenidate 在化学上比 amphetamine 更接近 cocaine。有一本旧书（2006 年）叫《Speed, Ecstasy, Ritalin: The Science of Amphetamines》，如果你想了解更详细的内容，挺有意思的。 > 大概吧~ 一开始我有四五天有点嗨，但实际上那非常让人分心，因为我会做一些疯狂的事，比如在淋浴时摔倒，因为感觉太舒服了，我都没法集中注意力。那个淋浴间刚修好，我差点又把它弄坏了。哈哈，我还因为 amphetamine 引发的过度热情大扫除，弄坏过一台冰柜和我自己的 PC。 > 总很高兴听到有人……
